name: Godric Renshaw
source_profile:
Duke Godric Renshaw, House Renshaw 
An aging, formidable southern aristocrat, Godric descends from one of Cador's oldest noble 
families. His house possesses extensive agricultural estates and maintains close relationships 
with several of the kingdom's most prestigious knightly orders. Godric was a principal supporter 
of the former king and strongly favored the restrictions on noble birthright. He considers 
northern merchant families unworthy of standing alongside the ancient aristocracy. 
Nevertheless, he remained loyal to Dedericus IV after the young king ascended the throne. He 
is too disciplined and politically experienced to openly challenge the monarch, but privately 
regards many of the king's reconciliatory policies as dangerous concessions. Godric is neither a 
coward nor an incompetent lord. His soldiers are well-trained, his estates are prosperous, and 
his personal commitment to duty is genuine.  
 
Political tension: Valmont represents the conservative old guard of southern Cador. Godric 
believes the crown should have used its victory to permanently curtail northern political 
influence. He might see the elevation of southern nobles such as Garrus Ashford and Cedric 
Bellamy as welcome, but regard their newly created titles as inferior to his ancient ducal 
authority. 
The Fallen Duchy of Duskfell 
An ancient ducal seat held by the Fallen House of Duskfell, but now lies in ruin due to a calamity 
that befell the duchy during the War of Broken Banners. This calamity, the Silence of Duskfell, 

resulted in the abandonment of its principal settlements and the disappearance of its ruling 
family. 
 
Before the war, Duskfell was one of the ancient southern duchies of Cador, ruled for centuries 
by House Mourne. Its lands were dominated by rugged hills, ancient woodlands, fertile valleys, 
and fortified settlements guarding important approaches to the royal heartland. Although less 
wealthy than the Duchy of Cade or Valemont, Duskfell enjoyed considerable prestige owing to 
its ancient lineage and military traditions.  
 
Its ruling lady, Duchess Aveline Mourne, was a proud and formidable aristocrat who maintained 
close ties to the southern knightly orders. House Mourne had long defended the kingdom's 
interior approaches, and its ancestral stronghold, Castle Vesper, guarded an important road 
toward Cade. This made the duchy a natural target for northern armies seeking to force the 
crown into negotiations. 
Fallen Duchess Aveline Mourne, House Mourne 
Duchess Aveline Mourne was the last recognized ruler of Duskfell. After the Silence of Duskfell, 
she disappeared and her ultimate fate remains unknown to all. Since then, the lands of Duskfell 
have fallen into ruin. The crown has never successfully established another ruling house there, 
and much of the territory remains effectively unclaimed.  
 
Political tension: The absence of a recognized ruler creates a peculiar legal situation. Several 
southern families may possess distant hereditary claims to the duchy, but none has successfully 
asserted authority over its lands. Some nobles might argue that Duskfell should be formally 
dissolved and its territory distributed among neighboring lordships. Others consider such a 
move an affront to the sanctity of hereditary titles. 
The Silence of Duskfell 
The common historical name of tragedy that befell the duchy is the Silence of Duskfell, however 
in poetry and folklore, the Still Night is commonly used as an equivalent. While much of its 
circumstances remain unknown, most accounts agree at least on the following.  
 
During the later stages of the civil war, northern forces launched a major offensive into southern 
Cador. The campaign was intended to threaten the royal heartland, divert southern armies from 
the northern territories, divide the southern territories and force King Dedericus III to negotiate 
from a position of weakness. 
 
Duskfell stood directly in their path. The duchess assembled her household knights, local levies, 
and the remaining garrisons of her duchy to resist the advancing armies.  However, the northern 
offensive was more successful than anticipated. Several outer fortresses fell, supply lines were 
severed, and much of Duskfell's countryside was overrun. Duchess Aveline ultimately withdrew 
to Castle Vesper, where she prepared to make her final stand.
